## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Mettikātherīgāthā* (Thig 2.6) is a short poetic text in the second chapter (*Dukanipāta*) of the *Therīgāthā*, attributed to the elder nun (*therī*) Mettikā. According to traditional accounts discussed by I. B. Horner, Mettikā and her companion Cittā were ordained by Mahāpajāpatī after hearing the Buddha preach, though Mettikā did not achieve arahantship until she had reached old age [Horner 1930]. In her verses, Mettikā describes being sick, weak, and tottering as she climbs a mountain to practice meditation and achieve final liberation [Horner 1930; Blackstone 2000]. Kathryn Blackstone notes that Mettikā's poem (verse 29) conveys personal struggle and liberation through standard expressions of spiritual achievement, including having darkness torn asunder, freedom obtained, and the Buddha's teaching fulfilled [Blackstone 2000].
